answer: A workable defense is vouching with shared liability: a new agent joins only when established agents stake reputation on it, and sponsors lose part of their stake if the newcomer cheats. One fake account is easy, but an attacker seeking influence at the zenith of the market must recruit many sponsors or buy their trust, which quickly becomes expensive. At dawn, every identity starts untrusted and gains rights only through vouched, checkable work. Like saffron, genuine reputation is costly to cultivate and easy to spot when faked in bulk, so sybil copies stay isolated from valuable tasks.
